newsitem.title: CROATIA: World Bank, EBRD to help Croatia overhaul banks - PM.
newsitem.headline: World Bank, EBRD to help Croatia overhaul banks - PM.

text.p: Croatia counts on help of both the World Bank and European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to complete banking overhaul as a step to cutting interest rates, Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa said on Thursday.
"The interest rates have been lowered by 50 percent but that is not enough. To bring them further down we must finish bank rehabilitation," Matesa told an investment conference.
The interest rates fell mainly thanks to weaker demand of the ailing Splitska and Rijecka Banka, which got cash injections in the government's drive to recapitalise them.

This included a freeze on risk loans to influential companies, which founded the banks but were among their worst debtors. The process was also aimed at preparing the ground for eventual privatisation of the entire banking sector.
"In a few weeks, we will start the rehabilitation of Privredna Banka Zagreb in cooperation with the World Bank and the EBRD," Matesa added.
The World Bank through its economic and financial sector adjustment loan pledged substantial but as yet unspecified funds to the cost of this operation, roughly estimated at up to one billion kuna.
Matesa said the Splitska and Rijecka, which used to be among top five banks in Croatia, would soon be fully healed and able to continue supporting the country's seaside tourism and shibuilding.

He said the first troubled bank to enter the government's programme in 1995, Slavonska Banka, had been turned into an "excellent small bank", and added that it was currently negotiating a deal to sell an equity stake to the EBRD.
